status: approved Rust slice only; TS activation remains separate
author: Mencius
decision: Reject atomic group settlement because it can lose an already completed scalar outcome at a shared deadline. Use exactly-two contiguous queued prefix siblings and streamed individual identity-bound responses; first response flushes after its postcheck, before second execution. Existing scalar path unchanged.

wireContract.rules: Exactly two monotonically increasing numeric-string child requestIds, shared epoch, no extra/null fields. Validate both complete bodies and eligibility before RPC. Reserve IDs once. Bounded pair line bytes <=1048576; large requests stay scalar at future client. No implicit fallback/retry of rejected groups.
wireContract.eligibility: Both pinned inner trial-prefix read requests; no preCalls, tokenDeals, native balance override, observations or effects. Equal endpoint/block/pin/root, complete trialPrefix incl code/input, from/origin/caller mode/gas limits. Different main target/data/stateRead allowed. Family names/addresses never drive eligibility.
wireContract.response: Existing scalar response envelopes, each with its original child identity and existing source/strict attestation. Flush A after bridge validation then execute B; never hold A until B finishes. Exact group-invalid validation error reporting must be deterministic and execute nothing. All physical fatal evidence still wins and bars later execution.

execution: Full pre(A): same three calls, fresh verified source.
Execute A using unchanged strict_simulate_at from fresh local state.
Bridge: post(A)+all three pre(B) checks in one physical HTTP batch (four logical calls; no dedup). Batch RPC items need not execute in server order, but all lie after execution A and before B.

Validate canonical post(A) and complete source B with existing header/profile semantics. Emit and flush A's ordinary outcome, preserving validation/execution errors and attestation rules. Source/protocol failures stay fail-closed.
Execute B from its own fresh local state, using its newly obtained one-use precheck evidence, never A's precheck result. Existing source-value cache remains as before.
Perform normal fresh canonical post(B) on success/revert/halt/ordinary error before emitting B.
Factor shared parsing/check/execution helpers where needed; no parallel EVM, journal reuse, trace hints or cached verification. Scalar behavior and existing guards must remain covered unchanged.
diagnostics: Use group-owned timing for bridge and physical attempts once, identify numeric child IDs and logical validation count. Do not nest/reset the scalar accumulator incorrectly or attribute all shared work to A and report B precheck as free. Preserve scalar diagnostics; killed group incomplete remains censored. No credentials/calldata/remote messages.
testsRequired: Two independent request outputs/gas/effects/attestations equal scalar execution including warm/transient isolation and ordinary failures
Exactly8 logical canonical calls over3 physical batches vs scalar4 physical; no check omitted, post retained on all outcomes
Bad source/hash/root/profile/chain and bridge/post errors, reordered/missing/duplicate RPC item IDs, physical fatal/throttle
Malformed group/IDs/bounds/noneligible contexts do no RPC; scalar unchanged
First response emitted before starting second execution, group partial failure does not fabricate success for second
Safe diagnostic accounting with no double count and disabled diagnostics no work
Full Rust tests, release build and diffcheck
authority: No TS/Family/main edits, no real RPC/live/env/process control, no commit/push/merge/deploy. Tests may use local stub HTTP. Main will review exact Rust diff before authorizing separate TS slice and any real test. If preserving contracts needs a broader change, report instead of weakening them.
